title.en: Solving linear inequalities on the number line

hook.en: An equation usually has one answer. An inequality has a whole ray of answers, and the *number line* shows it best.
hook.kn: ಸಮೀಕರಣಕ್ಕೆ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಒಂದೇ ಉತ್ತರ. ಅಸಮತೆಗೆ ಉತ್ತರಗಳ ಒಂದು ಪೂರ್ತಿ ಕಿರಣವೇ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ; ಸಂಖ್ಯಾರೇಖೆ ಅದನ್ನು ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Solution set and the number line

body.en: The *solution set* is all values of $x$ that make the inequality true; it depends on whether $x$ is in $N$, $Z$ or $R$. For real $x$ we draw it on the number line: a filled circle when the end point is included ($\le$, $\ge$), an open circle when it is not ($<$, $>$), and a thick ray in the direction of the solutions.
body.kn: ಪರಿಹಾರ ಗಣವು x ಯಾವ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಗಳಾಗಿರಬಹುದು ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದೆ. ಸಂಖ್ಯಾರೇಖೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ತುಂಬಿದ ವೃತ್ತ: ಅಂತ್ಯಬಿಂದು ಸೇರಿದೆ; ಖಾಲಿ ವೃತ್ತ: ಸೇರಿಲ್ಲ.

problem.en: Solve (2x − 1)/3 ≥ (3x − 2)/4 − (2 − x)/5 and show it on the number line.

steps.en: −17x ≥ −34 ⇒ x ≤ 2. Filled circle at 2, ray to the left.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Solve (2x − 1)/3 ≥ (3x − 2)/4 − (2 − x)/5 and show it on the number line.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Solve 2x minus 1/3 is greater than or equal to 3x minus 2/4 - (2 - x)/5 and show it on the number line.
Multiply by the LCM 60: 202x minus 1 is greater than or equal to 153x minus 2 minus 12(2 - x).
40x minus 20 is greater than or equal to 45x minus 30 minus 24 plus 12x equals 57x minus 54.
minus 17x is greater than or equal to minus 34 so x is less than or equal to 2. Filled circle at 2, ray to the left.
So the answer is x is less than or equal to 2, that is (- infinity, 2].

problem.en: Solve 24x < 100 when x is (i) a natural number, (ii) an integer.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Solve 24x < 100 when x is (i) a natural number, (ii) an integer.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Solve 24x is less than 100 when x is i a natural number, ii an integer.
x is less than 100 over 24 equals 25 over 6 is approximately 4.17.
i Natural numbers: {1, 2, 3, 4}.
ii Integers: {..., minus 2, minus 1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4}.
So the answer is i {1, 2, 3, 4}; ii {..., minus 1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4}.
